subject.title: fix(ui): reject nondecimal strings in config form number coercion

question: Should generic Control UI number fields continue accepting scientific notation such as `1e5`, which native number controls already accept and which is numerically equivalent to `100000`?
rationale: The patch intentionally turns an existing accepted numeric entry form into a schema error, and the nearby cron-specific precedent does not settle the generic config-form compatibility contract.

options.title: Preserve scientific notation
options.body: Accept finite exponent notation for number fields while retaining rejection of radix-prefixed and other non-decimal JavaScript spellings.

options.title: Adopt plain-decimal-only entry
options.body: Keep the proposed grammar and document that Control UI config fields intentionally reject exponent notation despite native number-input support.

recommendation.title: Preserve scientific notation
recommendation.body: Accept finite exponent notation for number fields while retaining rejection of radix-prefixed and other non-decimal JavaScript spellings.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged Control UI numeric-parser work is the closest concrete precedent for deciding the intended grammar.
